correctness.rationale: For centrally symmetric K, ℓ(y)=ℓ(-y) is even. By definition the λ-Steiner fiber is [-λℓ(y),(1-λ)ℓ(y)]. If the symmetral is centrally symmetric, uniqueness of the center of its projected body forces symmetry center tu; reflected fibers give 2t=(1-2λ)ℓ(y). The nonzero factor for 0≤λ<1/2 forces a common positive length L. Lower/upper chord-boundary functions are convex and sum -L, making each affine and giving K as a prism F+[0,L]u. Conversely constant-length chords give a product P×[-λL,(1-λ)L] after graph shear, centrally symmetric. Facet pairs are countable by finite boundary measure, with at most ±u for each prism facet translation, so symmetry-preserving directions are countable. Affine equivalence to the original centrally symmetric K would preserve symmetry for every u, contradicting this countability. Conclusion concerns centrally symmetric class, not all bodies.
